t: Plates Between Candles — Precompute Candle Anchors for O(1) Queries
o: A row of plates '*' and candles '|' is probed by range queries: for substring [left, right], count plates that have at least one candle on BOTH sides within that substring. Equivalently, only the plates lying between the first candle at-or-after left and the last candle at-or-before right count. Example 1 (s = "**|**|***|"): query [2,5] encloses candles at indices 2 and 5 with plates 3 and 4 in between — answer 2; query [5,9] encloses candles 5 and 9 with plates 6,7,8 — answer 3. In Example 2, [1,17] yields 9 while the other four ranges lack an enclosing candle pair and yield 0. With |s| and |queries| up to 100000, rescanning each substring is far too slow; precompute plate counts once (prefix sums) plus a fast way to jump to enclosing candles, then answer every query in O(1) or O(log |s|).
k: A query's answer depends only on two anchor candles: the FIRST candle >= left and the LAST candle <= right; interior candles are irrelevant.
Prefix sums of '*' turn any segment's plate count into one subtraction.
Nearest-candle-left/right arrays give true O(1) queries; binary searching a sorted candle-position list gives O(log |s|) — both are linear-time preprocessing.

a.n: Approach 1: Prefix Sums + Binary Search over Candle Positions
a.i: Collect all candle indices into a sorted list and build prefix counts of plates. For a query, binary search the first candle index >= left and the last candle index <= right; if fewer than two distinct enclosing candles exist the answer is 0, otherwise subtract prefix sums between those two positions.
s: Record indices of every '|' in a sorted array; build prefix[i] = number of '*' before position i.
Per query, lo = index of first candle >= left via binary search.
hi = index of last candle <= right via binary search.
If lo >= hi there is no enclosing pair — answer 0.
Otherwise answer prefix[hi_pos + 1] - prefix[lo_pos] over the two candle positions.
a.t: O(|s| + q log |s|) — linear preprocessing, then two binary searches per query.
a.sp: O(|s|) — the candle-position list and the prefix array.

a.n: Approach 2: Nearest-Candle Arrays for O(1) per Query
a.i: Trade the binary searches for two lookup tables built in one sweep each: left[i] = nearest candle at or before i, right[i] = nearest candle at or after i. A query then reads its anchors directly — right[left] and left[right] — and subtracts prefix sums, making every query constant time.
s: Sweep left to right building prefix plate counts and left[i] (nearest candle at or before i).
Sweep right to left filling right[i] (nearest candle at or after i).
Per query take a = right[left], b = left[right].
Answer 0 unless a < b (both anchors exist and are distinct).
a.t: O(|s| + q) — constant work per query after two linear sweeps.
a.sp: O(|s|) — prefix counts plus the two nearest-candle arrays.

w: Use Approach 2 when queries dominate (its per-query cost is unbeatable); Approach 1 wins when memory is tight or the candle list must be shared across query batches. Pitfalls: counting ALL plates in [left, right] instead of only those inside the anchor candles; forgetting that TWO distinct candles are required (strictly a < b); off-by-one errors when the substring boundary itself is a plate. Edge cases worth testing: ranges of all candles (answer 0), a single-candle range, queries touching both string ends. Follow-up: point updates flipping plates/candles — replace prefix sums with a Fenwick tree and keep the anchor logic.
